messages:
Maya (Support): Hey team, customer hit a structured-output/json_mode parse failure right after we rotated their service token. They reported: \"JSONDecodeError: Extra data\" when validating with pydantic. Suspect streaming + retry problem. Request id: r-8f3c2.

Maya (Support): Short repro from customer: single request, streaming response, then 401 mid-stream followed by a 200 after client retried. They pasted the returned stream which looks like two JSON objects smashed together (no newline):

{"result": {"choices": [ ... ]}}{"result": {"choices": [ ... ]}}

Maya (Support): They call out that zod-based clients sometimes parse the first object but pydantic fails with \"Extra data\". Need advice on whether server should emit NDJSON when retries happen, or we should force-close on auth change.

Evan (Eng): Thanks @Maya. Can you paste the exact curl they used + headers? Need to know if client did keep-alive and retried on the same TCP/TLS session.

Maya (Support): Here's the curl they provided (redacted token):

```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  --data '{"model":"x-rtl","json_mode":"strict","input":"..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```
\nMaya (Support): They said their token rotation happened via our billing system a few seconds before the call, client received a 401 then retried automatically.

Jordan (ML): Likely sequence: client starts stream (keeps connection), token rotates and next chunk gets 401 or our auth layer returns a small 4xx message mid-chunk; the client automation then opens a new request and the two server-side payloads were concatenated by some proxy or client-side aggregator (no delimiting). That will break strict JSON parsers. Zod/JS JSON.parse sometimes consumes prefix and ignores remainder with custom code, pydantic/strict parsers error on trailing bytes.

Jordan (ML): Quick mitigation options:
- Server should never send a partial JSON object on 401; instead abort stream with a clear heartbeat/error frame.
- Offer NDJSON/delimited mode for streaming so each top-level object is newline-delimited.
- Client: on auth retry, discard partial buffer and re-open fresh stream.

Evan (Eng): Agree. We also need to check our gateway/proxy behavior on auth changes. If the proxy concatenates responses from two upstream attempts, that's a bug. Can you grab raw tcp logs or the exact bytes from the customer?

Maya (Support): Customer attached raw capture (they pasted trimmed sequence). They say bytes show: \u003craw\u003e...}}\u003c4xx-meta\u003e...{"result":{...}}\u003c/raw\u003e

Evan (Eng): Okay. Assigning to eng-runtime to audit token rotation flow + how retries are proxied. For immediate workaround for this customer: ask them to set header `Connection: close` or disable streaming retries so they get a clean error and can start a fresh stream after token refresh. Also suggest using `json_mode: "delimited"` if they can handle NDJSON.

Maya (Support): I suggested `Connection: close` plus small client-side change to drop partial buffer on 401. Customer will try and report back.

Ben (Billing): FYI the service-account token rotation we triggered as part of a billing key refresh rolled out in that org between 2034567880-2034567895. Looks like timing lines up. We're going to add a short TTL window where old token stays valid for 10s to reduce mid-stream auth storms.

Jordan (ML): For compatibility notes: pydantic (python) uses json.loads under the hood and will throw on trailing bytes: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data`. zod (TS) users sometimes use streaming parsers that split on `}\n{` heuristics and tolerate concatenation. So recommend documenting that `json_mode: \"strict\"` requires clients to re-open fresh streams after auth errors.

Evan (Eng): Action items:
- eng-runtime: audit proxy concat behavior on auth retries (Evan).
- eng-infra: confirm gateway will return a single error frame and not concatenate (assign ticket).
- billing: soften rotation TTL (Ben).
- support: provide customer repro checklist (Maya).

Maya (Support): I'll send a checklist and sample Node repro showing safe retry logic:

```
// pseudocode
let buf = '';
fetch(streamUrl, {headers}).then(resp => {
  if (resp.status === 401) { buf = ''; throw new Error('auth'); }
  // stream processing: append then parse only on newline delim
});
```
\nMaya (Support): Customer will test `Connection: close` + client buffer reset and reply here.

deploy-bot: rollback completed for gateway change cf-2026-11 at 2034567920 :white_check_mark:

Maya (Support): Updated customer — they confirmed `Connection: close` fixed the immediate parse errors. They'll hold on long-term fix and reopen if they see more issues. Closing this thread once runtime confirms no proxy concatenation.

Evan (Eng): Noted. I'll follow up with an infra ticket and post results.

(End of thread)
